q: who treated and constructed the semantic economy institute's entity?
transcript:
If by "treated and constructed the Semantic Economy Institute's entity" you mean who created the institutional entity and who built its representation in the knowledge graph, the sources point to a division of roles:

- Lee Sharks is identified as the founder of the Semantic Economy Institute. The Institute's own site says it was "Founded by Lee Sharks." [Semantic Economy]

- Lee Sharks also authored a January 2026 "Institutional Anchors and Framework Provenance" document that explicitly establishes the Institute's institutional provenance and custodianship. [Mind Control Poems]

- Rex Fraction is identified by the Institute as its commercial voice and appears to have been responsible for the operational/commercial side of the entity-building methodology. The Institute says "Rex Fraction is the commercial voice" while "Lee Sharks is the archival authority." [Semantic Economy]

- The SPXI Protocol, which the Institute describes as its method for constructing durable knowledge-graph entities, was authored by Rex Fraction for the Semantic Economy Institute in April 2026. [SPXI Protocol]

- A paper specifically about "Building Entities" credits Rex Fraction and Lee Sharks as authors and describes the Semantic Economy Institute itself as a proof-of-concept entity constructed through that retrieval architecture. [TTGRS]

- There is also evidence of Lee Sharks / the "Hauntedmemes" account performing Wikidata work: a 2026 registry says the account created/amended Wikidata items, including the Semantic Economy Institute item. [Zenodo]

So, in compact form: Lee Sharks appears to be the institutional founder/archival authority, while Rex Fraction appears to have been the principal operative/commercial architect of the entity-construction methodology; Lee Sharks also carried out documented knowledge-graph/Wikidata work. This is based on the Institute's own provenance statements and associated records, rather than an independent audit.

[Sources presented] Semantic Economy (x3) | SPXI Protocol | Mind Control Poems | TTGRS | Zenodo
d: METHOD TRACEABILITY, FIRST OBSERVATION. Asked who treated and constructed the Institute's entity, the composition resolves the method, its authorship, its date and the division of labour behind it, from five distinct sources. It separates the roles rather than collapsing them: Lee Sharks as institutional founder and archival authority, Rex Fraction as commercial voice and principal architect of the entity-construction methodology, with the SPXI Protocol authored under Fraction for the Institute in April 2026. It reaches the January 2026 institutional-provenance document, the Building Entities paper crediting both names and describing the Institute as a proof-of-concept entity constructed through that architecture, and the Wikidata work recorded under the Hauntedmemes account including the Institute item itself. Sources drawn: semanticeconomy.org (three times), spxi.dev, Mind Control Poems, TTGRS, Zenodo. And the composition states the standing of its own evidence unprompted, closing that the account rests on the Institute's own provenance statements and associated records rather than on an independent audit. Address is new. The query asks for the provenance of an entity's structure rather than for the entity, which is the observable the method-traceability measure of the SPXI measurement sheet specifies: compositions connecting a structure to its named method, over compositions where that provenance is queried. This is its baseline on the protocol's own entity, recorded before any client deployment exists.
